# <b>DIOCESAN COLLECTIVE WORSHIP FRAMEWORK</b>

| Lord Jesus we<br />meet today in<br />your name;<br /><b>help us to<br />come closer<br />to you, Father<br />God; and be<br />filled with<br />your Holy<br />Spirit.</b>   | <b>CREATING CHANGE IN THE WORLD (whole school)</b><br /><b>Matthew 6 v 19-21</b><br />Discuss the inequalities in the world and where/why/how they have come about and why it<br />can be difficult to change them. Use the stories of real children and families around the<br />world to demonstrate this – there are some examples on<br />http://www.christianaid.org.uk/resources/games/stories/index.aspx<br />Also talk about what is really important in life (Matthew 6 v 19-21) – by reading about<br />children whose lives are different from ours and who cannot take safety or the basic<br />needs of life for granted as we do, pupils should be encouraged to think about what has<br />true value.<br />Make sure that you focus for prayer today is on change for those who are our neighbours<br />around the world and who need our prayers to bring about positive change.                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                           | others so very little. Help us to<br />stand up for what is right and to<br />be people of love and<br />generosity. Loving God, show<br />us your way.   | your Holy Spirit on<br />his disciples, and<br />empowering people<br />of every nation<br />through the<br />centuries.<br />Enlighten us by the<br />power of that Spirit<br />so that we may<br />speak your praise<br />and tell others of<br />your saving work<br />through Jesus Christ<br />our Lord<br /><b>Amen</b><br />May the mind of<br />Christ my Saviour<br />live in me from day to<br />day.<br />By his love and<br />power controlling<br />all I do or say   |

|                                                                                                                                                                              | <b>PRAYER CAN CHANGE ME AND CHANGE OTHERS</b><br /><b>Matthew 6 v 7-8</b><br />This is a creative way to encourage children to pray out loud in a group. This game gives<br />them a framework in which to pray and have fun.<br />You’ll need a noughts and crosses grid, big enough for everyone to see and six cards with<br />P on and six with T on. For younger children you could make the cards different colours<br />so they can tell at a glance which is which.<br />Divide the group into two teams and play the game like a normal game of noughts and<br />crosses, placing the cards on the grid in turn to try to make a line. But before you can put<br />a card down, you say a Please prayer if you’re on the P team or a Thank you prayer if<br />you’re on the T team. Swap over at the end of a game to have a return match.<br />Variations: With older children you might focus the game more by providing a newspaper<br />for each team and specifying that they should pray for and about items in the paper. With<br />younger children you could have symbols or pictures as stimulus for prayer on each side:<br />pictures of sick people, the weather, animals, a cross, a candle, a dove, things of natural<br />beauty, food, houses, someone crying, local schools etc<br />You could specify that all the prayers should be about something that’s happened in the<br />past week (the Ts) or that will happen in the coming week (the Ps).<br />(courtesy of ‘Barnabas in Churches’) |                                                                                                                                                           |                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                                    |
